description: Whether a text holds a token a cabinet issued, and which: a managed copy (settings.json, CLAUDE.md) or a session's transcript. Such a file is not pushed to the store: in a synced file a token would be in the store's history and its mirror for good. The public ids (tk_<id>) are what the person is told, to revoke each. Tokens here are synthetic: the secret is one repeated character, which no issued token is.

cases.note: The likeliest way a token gets into settings.json: an env block for an MCP config that reads it from the environment. The file must stay on the machine.
A hook command that calls the server with the token inline: the same file, the same leak.
A token glued to the text before it is still a token: the check looks for the shape anywhere, not for a whole word.
Words about the format are not a token: without eight characters of the id alphabet and the separator, nothing is withheld.
cases.text: Tokens look like vmt_<id>_<secret>; the id is eight characters.

cases.note: No cabinet issues an id with capitals or with i, l, o, u: such a string is not one of ours.
An id is exactly eight characters.
The public id alone — as it appears in a journal line or in the cabinet — opens nothing and may travel.
The token from before the cabinet is 64 hex characters, like any digest, and cannot be told apart by its shape; it is not looked for, and the spec says so.
Settings without a token are shared as always.
The likeliest way into a transcript: the agent read a settings file, and its content came back as a tool result. The transcript stays on the machine.
Every token is named, so each can be revoked.
A token pasted twice is one token to revoke.
